text:
Sam (People Ops): Member got a travel vaccine in Prague and clinic is asking if Redwood will direct-bill. They request payment to a Revolut IBAN and want the EOB sent with only codes+amounts to the member. Claim 2026-CZ-2102. Who owns flow and what docs do we need?

Ivy (Benefits): Benefits owns coverage check. Need signed Assignment of Benefits (AOB), itemized invoice with local procedure codes and dates, and patient consent for any redaction.

Luca (Finance): We can pay to a verified IBAN. Revolut is OK if provider supplies bank statement or proof-of-account and VAT/tax ID. Prefer USD wires if provider accepts, but IBAN in EUR works too.

Sam (People Ops): Can someone paste a one-line AOB and a super-short checklist I can forward to the clinic?

Ivy (Benefits): AOB: "I, [MemberName], assign benefits for claim 2026-CZ-2102 to [ProviderName] and authorize Redwood Inference to pay the provider directly." Checklist: 1) Signed AOB (PDF) 2) Itemized invoice (CZK/EUR) with codes & dates 3) Provider tax/VAT ID 4) Bank proof for IBAN (bank letter or statement) 5) Billing contact. Send to claims@redwood.com.

Luca (Finance): Add: "If paying to Revolut, include proof that IBAN belongs to the clinic (bank letter or recent remittance)." Also: international wires 3-7 business days after KYC.

ClaimsBot: Automated: International direct-bill flagged  manual review required. Expected adjudication 4-8 business days after complete docs.

Sam (People Ops): About the EOB redaction request: can we send member copy with only codes+amounts?

Ivy (Benefits): Member-facing copy can follow their consent. We must retain full EOB (names, dates) in claims file for audit. If member signs consent to initials-only, we can send limited copy.

Sam (People Ops): Great, forwarding now. Will update when clinic replies. :thumbsup: (end)
